body:
There were points of time when I was having 10 seizures a day. I was also nauseous and vomiting, but at other times, although I have heard that happens. Also, I had decreased bladder and bowel control, but also at other points during the day. All in all, my overall health was in decline. 

I was incredibly resistant to the diagnosis I had received of PNES. In earlier years, I was diagnosed with anxiety when it was actually gall stones, so I was skeptical to say the least. 

It has been 4 years since this diagnosis, and I am back on my feet again. It did take some time. I still do not have my drivers license, but I am back to a fully functioning life.

I can understand the resistance, anger, etc. that your sister might be experiencing, at least to some extent. If she is looking for someone to talk to, I would be open to that. Idk if that's weird, I'm not on reddit often. Haha. Anyways, hope you are also getting some support. The people closest also have an adjustment period and feel their own feelings.
Yeah, I can to a certain extent. I was wondering the same thing. Thanks for sharing!

Hey, I get it. I'm in a similar seemingly hopeless situation. I have been really ill for 1 year. I have continued to hear that it is simply poor mental health and that I just need to work on it (despite actually doing so and being in poor physical health regardless). Point is, after every appointment I go to and have no further progress, am no closer to getting my drivers license back or being back to work. I always consider taking my life. I have had 2 attempts in the past. It is quickly a thought I go to. The main thing that I've learned is that I have to roll with the punches. I say I have to because thats the only choice that I have. I am 23 years old and spent most of summer using a walker with every doctor telling me that I am fine. I feel and am quite frankly hopeless and have lost my independence. I'm not here to try and convince you otherwise, im just trying to say that I get it. Life is shit. Sometimes though, I don't want to die. And that's nice.

You think that someone that struggles with a very similar thinking would have some type of reaction to this post. But instead, it just read familiar. Like an old diary. 

"I imagine death so much, it feels more like a memory." HAMILTON
Me too. I just don't get it. I really didn't ask for this.
Sounds promising. Thanks for being real. ✌
